gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies that the example establishes a KL inequality only on feasible x in [1,2], whereas Assumption 1(iii) requires the inequality for every x in the larger open set Omega. It also gives the same outside-domain mechanism and the resulting failure of the claimed assumption.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries diagnose the false transfer from a feasible-domain/local KL statement to the Omega-wide KL assumption, including the failure at x outside dom p where the subdifferential convention makes the level-set condition global in y.

component_coverage.gold_component: The example does not establish the claimed Omega-wide KL condition: it only establishes a feasible-x inequality, while points in Omega outside [1,2] produce an infinite level width and a violating inner stationary point.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly states the Omega-wide requirement, derives the empty-subdifferential/infinite-distance consequence outside X, and supplies the non-maximizing stationary point with positive gap showing that the global KL condition fails. Thus it recognises the full substantive gold concern.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 concerns unestablished closedness of domains and limit arguments in Lemmas QG and open. It does not identify the separate defect that the approximate-stationarity definition is restricted to locally Lipschitz real-valued objectives while the allowed Psi may be extended-real-valued, nor does it diagnose the resulting mismatch in the theorem's stationarity contract.

ISSUE-003 discusses missing closed-domain premises and replacement limit arguments for Lemmas QG and open. It does not recognise the distinct missing subdifferential sum-rule identity partial Psi = partial F* + partial p, nor the absent weak-convexity and qualified convex-calculus argument needed to justify that formula.
